findings.title: Findings converge on `rest_request`'s retry loop under the delivery-state model
findings.why_it_matters: D6 maps REST failures onto the three delivery states inside `inner_request` but leaves the tenacity loop around it untouched ("REST retries ... stay as they are under every option"). That loop retries anything not in `NOT_RETRYABLE` and re-raises only the last attempt's exception. Under the new classes this one unchanged mechanism causes two separate problems. It re-sends REST writes after an outcome-unknown attempt, which contradicts D5's "retry follows delivery state" (Finding 3). And it reports the last attempt's class, so an earlier attempt that may have applied can come out as `CommandNotSentError` (Finding 2), the one class #3677 records as certain. The question for the user: does the REST retry loop need re-evaluating as part of this ledger, instead of being patched once per finding? That re-evaluation includes whether REST writes should retry an outcome-unknown attempt at all, and whether leaving the loop alone and documenting it is acceptable.
findings.recommended: A: Re-evaluate `rest_request`'s retry loop before addressing the converging findings individually. Open questions: should REST retry eligibility follow delivery state as D5 does for WebSocket? Does that differ for reads and writes? What class does a call report after several attempts? Is keeping today's loop and documenting it an acceptable outcome?
findings.chosen: A: Re-evaluate `rest_request`'s retry loop before addressing the converging findings individually. Open questions: should REST retry eligibility follow delivery state as D5 does for WebSocket? Does that differ for reads and writes? What class does a call report after several attempts? Is keeping today's loop and documenting it an acceptable outcome?
findings.choice_reason: Settled as new D8: GETs retry as today, other methods retry only CommandNotSentError. User: 'whatever the most proper setup is - thats one of the oldest lines of code, there is no reason to keep it the way it is.'

findings.title: A REST write retried after an unknown outcome can surface as `CommandNotSentError`
findings.why_it_matters: `rest_request` re-raises only the last attempt's exception (`reraise=True`). D6 maps per attempt. Suppose attempt 1 of a REST write times out or loses its connection after the POST went out (outcome unknown), and attempts 2 to 5 are refused because HA is restarting. The call then raises `CommandNotSentError`, which the ledger defines as "certain it never reached HA". #3677's D4 records that as `not_sent`, "the one outcome that's certain". So the record is wrong in exactly the outage case it exists for. WebSocket writes avoid this because they pass `retry_on_timeout=False`. REST writes have no equivalent.
findings.recommended: A: Don't retry a REST non-GET request after an outcome-unknown failure (key `is_retryable_rest_failure` on the new classes and the method).

findings.title: REST outcome-unknown writes are still retried, contradicting D5's retry-follows-delivery-state rule
findings.why_it_matters: D6 maps inside `inner_request`, so the retry predicate sees `ResponseTimeoutError`/`ResponseLostError`. Neither is in `NOT_RETRYABLE`, so both are retried up to `MAX_RETRY_ATTEMPTS`. A REST POST that timed out is re-sent up to five times, and the final error still says "the command may or may not have applied". On WebSocket the same class is never retried for writes. So one class gets opposite retry semantics depending on the transport, and #3677's single row per call hides up to five sends. `delete_entity` re-sent after an applied first attempt gets a 404, which #3677 records as `rejected` for a delete that actually succeeded.
findings.recommended: A: Key `is_retryable_rest_failure` on delivery state: never retry `OutcomeUnknownError` for non-GET methods. Not-sent and retryable statuses stay retried.

findings.title: D6's connect-timeout → not-sent mapping can't happen under the project's REST timeout config
findings.why_it_matters: D6 and the Assumed section say aiohttp raises `ConnectionTimeoutError` "when `connector.connect` times out", and map it to not-sent. That only happens when `ClientTimeout.connect` or `sock_connect` is set. `rest_request` passes `ClientTimeout(total=...)` per request. That replaces the session default, which is aiohttp's `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT` with `sock_connect=30`, so the override actually removes the connect bound aiohttp would otherwise apply. With `connect=None`, `ceil_timeout(None)` is a no-op. The 30 s total timer then cancels the task inside `connector.connect`, and `TimerContext.__exit__` turns that into a plain `TimeoutError` outside `_connect_and_send_request`'s `except asyncio.TimeoutError`. D6 files a plain `TimeoutError` as outcome-unknown. So a host that silently drops packets produces "may have applied" for a request that never connected, and #3677 records it as `connection_lost`. As written, the ledger promises a split the code can't produce. The error is in the safe direction, though: it claims less than is known.
findings.recommended: A: Set a `sock_connect` bound on `rest_request`'s default `ClientTimeout` (a module-level constant), so connect-phase timeouts raise `ConnectionTimeoutError` → `CommandNotSentError` as D6 already states.
findings.chosen: A: Set a `sock_connect` bound on `rest_request`'s default `ClientTimeout` (a module-level constant), so connect-phase timeouts raise `ConnectionTimeoutError` → `CommandNotSentError` as D6 already states.

findings.title: D6 silently breaks catches of builtin `OSError`/`TimeoutError` around REST calls, which D2's own deciding factor rules out
findings.why_it_matters: D2 rejects keeping `FailedMessageError` because a narrowed meaning under an unchanged name is a silent break. D6 creates the same kind of silent break for REST. Today `ClientConnectorError` is an `OSError`, and a REST timeout is the builtin `TimeoutError`. After D6, both become `HassetteError`-only classes. So `except (OSError, TimeoutError)` or `except TimeoutError` around `api.get_state`, `get_history` or `set_state` stops catching, and no import error warns anyone. The docs taught exactly this: `catch_ha_unreachable.py` catches `aiohttp.ClientError, TimeoutError`. D6's accepted-cost sentence names only `aiohttp.ClientError`, so the BREAKING footer would miss the builtin catches. (hautomate survives only because its `RECOVERABLE_HA_ERRORS` also lists `HassetteError`.) A smaller wording issue: D6 also raises `CommandNotSentError` and "the command may or may not have applied" messages on REST *reads*.
findings.recommended: A: Name builtin `OSError`/`TimeoutError` catches around REST calls in D6's accepted cost and the BREAKING footer, and show the replacement in the rewritten `catch_ha_unreachable.py` snippet.
findings.chosen: A: Name builtin `OSError`/`TimeoutError` catches around REST calls in D6's accepted cost and the BREAKING footer, and show the replacement in the rewritten `catch_ha_unreachable.py` snippet.

findings.title: `ResourceNotReadyError` is certainly not sent but stays outside the not-sent class, so #3677 mislabels it
findings.why_it_matters: `inner_request` raises `ResourceNotReadyError` before any network I/O when the REST session is down. That makes it the purest not-sent case. The ledger keeps it out of scope. #3677's REST mapping has no rule for it ("failed connect → `not_sent`; ... any other failure → `connection_lost`"), so a write that never left the process is recorded as "sent, then the connection ended". The WebSocket equivalent (the readiness check in `Api.ws_send_*`) raises `CommandNotSentError` under this ledger, so the same state gets different classes on the two transports. That breaks the Summary's "one delivery-state model across both transports". It is also a `HassetteError` rather than a `RuntimeError`, so it is retried five times with backoff, as it is today.
findings.recommended: A: Raise `CommandNotSentError` at `inner_request`'s closed-session check, and list the change in the BREAKING footer.
findings.chosen: A: Raise `CommandNotSentError` at `inner_request`'s closed-session check, and list the change in the BREAKING footer.

findings.title: A drain-time failure is reported as not-sent, although aiohttp already raises a different class for it
findings.why_it_matters: D4 maps `ClientConnectionResetError`, `ConnectionError` and `OSError` from the socket write to not-sent. It accepts the drain case as a documented edge, on the reasoning that telling the cases apart would take message-text matching. In hassette's configuration the class already separates them. Hassette calls `ws_connect` without compression (aiohttp's default `compress=0`), so the frame write is synchronous. Before that write, `ClientConnectionResetError` is raised by `send_frame`'s closing check or `_write_websocket_frame`'s `transport.is_closing()` check, which means the frame was certainly not written. The drain wait, by contrast, fails with a plain `ConnectionError("Connection lost")` that `connection_lost` sets on the drain waiter. `_drain_helper`'s own `ClientConnectionResetError` branch needs `transport is None`, and that can't happen right after a synchronous write that just checked `is_closing()`. So the ledger's Situation and Assumed bullet are inaccurate: the drain case does not raise `ClientConnectionResetError`. The senior engineer also noted that the drain failure fires at the moment the connection dies, while #3677's `fail_all` resolves the same entry. Both #3677 writers then update one row. In practice the caller's `not_sent` lands last, which is the outcome D4 already accepts.
findings.recommended: B: Accept as a known limitation: a drain-time connection loss with a queued frame is reported as not-sent (correct D4's Situation and Assumed to say the drain wait raises a plain `ConnectionError`, not `ClientConnectionResetError`).
findings.chosen: B: Accept as a known limitation: a drain-time connection loss with a queued frame is reported as not-sent (correct D4's Situation and Assumed to say the drain wait raises a plain `ConnectionError`, not `ClientConnectionResetError`).
findings.choice_reason: Batch first applied option A (class-based split); user then reverted: 'I don't want to be tied to their internals and I think the rare case is fine.'

findings.title: REST failures after the response headers arrive are outside D6's mapping
findings.why_it_matters: `rest_request` returns the `ClientResponse` once the headers arrive. Callers read the body (`await response.json()`) outside the `except` chain D6 extends. A disconnect or timeout during the body read still raises a raw `aiohttp.ClientError`/`TimeoutError`. That contradicts "one delivery-state model across both transports", and the docs would tell users the aiohttp catch is no longer needed. For a write, HA has already answered with a status by that point, so the command was processed.
findings.recommended: B: Accept as a known limitation: REST mapping covers failures up to the response headers; a body-read failure raises raw `aiohttp`/`TimeoutError`.
findings.chosen: B: Accept as a known limitation: REST mapping covers failures up to the response headers; a body-read failure raises raw `aiohttp`/`TimeoutError`.

findings.title: A retried WebSocket read reports its last attempt's class
findings.why_it_matters: under D5, `send_and_wait` with `retry_on_timeout=True` retries a `ResponseTimeoutError`. Suppose the connection drops before the retry. The next attempt hits the closed send gate, raises `CommandNotSentError`, and isn't retried. So a call whose first attempt may have reached HA ends as "not sent". This is the same last-attempt problem as Finding 2, but here it is harmless for idempotent reads, and every built-in write passes `retry_on_timeout=False`. `ws_send_and_wait` is public, though, and defaults to `True`.
findings.recommended: A: Add a docstring sentence: after retries, the raised class describes the last attempt, so a not-sent after an earlier timeout doesn't prove the command never reached HA (pass `retry_on_timeout=False` for writes).
findings.chosen: A: Add a docstring sentence: after retries, the raised class describes the last attempt, so a not-sent after an earlier timeout doesn't prove the command never reached HA (pass `retry_on_timeout=False` for writes).

findings.title: The ledger doesn't say the existing log context survives D4 and D7
findings.why_it_matters: today `send_json` logs the command label (ERROR on reset, `logger.exception` on any other failure). D4 stops wrapping non-connection exceptions. Unless the build keeps those lines, an unattended app's raw `TypeError` from an unserializable payload arrives without the command label. D7 has REST timeouts raise `ResponseTimeoutError`. The WebSocket raise site's message hardcodes `RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (15 s), while REST's deadline is the configurable `rest_request_timeout_seconds` (30 s default). The message is built at each raise site, so this is only a risk if the build copies the WebSocket message. Stating it once avoids a "no response within 15s" line for a REST call.
findings.chosen: In D4's Recommendation, add one sentence: "`send_json` keeps its existing log lines with the command label, both for the not-sent case and for an exception it lets propagate unwrapped." In D7's Recommendation, add: "Each raise site's message names its own deadline: REST timeouts cite the configured `rest_request_timeout_seconds`, not `RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`." Set D4's and D7's `**Ratified:**` to `pending` per the resolution flow.

findings.title: The build's file list misses `api/REVIEW.md`
findings.why_it_matters: the "New pieces" Docs list names about 12 files, but not `src/hassette/api/REVIEW.md`. Lines 16-17 of that file ask about `except FailedMessageError` and the rewrap that erases the type, and both go stale after D2 and the re-parenting. A review-questions staleness check would flag it after the build. The other items the critic listed are already covered: the Summary's "every raise site, `except` site and retry predicate in `src/`" covers `NOT_RETRYABLE`'s `ConnectionClosedError` entry, the Assumed `_ws_helper_call` bullet covers the comment at `api.py:207`, the D3 rename covers `RetryableConnectionClosedError`'s `__all__` entry, and the Posture leaves hautomate's comment to a separate update.
findings.chosen: Append `src/hassette/api/REVIEW.md` (the `FailedMessageError` review questions) to the Docs bullet in the Summary's "New pieces" list.
